fields.meta_title: Conference Registration Form With Session Picks | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a conference registration form that prices passes by date, closes full breakouts and saves every attendee to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Conference Registration Form Around Your Agenda
fields.hero_description: Describe your program and what each pass costs. Emergent builds a conference registration form that knows which sessions are full and what each attendee owes.
fields.features_heading: What a Conference Registration Has to Carry
fields.features_subheading: A conference sells several passes across several days. These six parts keep the attendee list and the invoices in agreement.
fields.feature_1:
Different sections per attendee type

Ask speakers for a bio and a headshot, exhibitors for booth size and power, and attendees for neither. Emergent builds one form that branches on the registration type picked first.
fields.feature_2:
Badge names checked before printing

Collect each name and company exactly as they should print, with a length limit that fits the badge. Export the badge list as a CSV for the printer in the week before doors open.
fields.feature_3:
Fees taken as part of registering

Connect Stripe or any processor with an API and take the pass price at submit. A registration stays pending until payment clears, and a refund marks that attendee as canceled.
fields.feature_4:
Agenda emails after every change

Send each attendee a confirmation listing the sessions they picked, with a link to swap them. Schedule a reminder two days before the opening keynote with venue and check-in details.
fields.feature_5:
Every attendee as a row you own

Keep each attendee's pass and session picks in a database you own, beside their payment status. Filter by track for a headcount per room, or sync every attendee into HubSpot.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

Publish the form on the conference site's own domain or embed it on a page you already run. Export the full code to GitHub when developers want registration inside their app.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Rules a Conference Form Runs On
fields.tab_content_1:
A full room takes its breakout off the form

Afternoons at the Fieldwork Summit split into four breakouts, and each attendee picks one. Room 204 seats 60. When the 60th attendee chooses the pricing teardown, that session drops off the form and the program team gets a Slack message. The other three sessions stay open with their seat counts showing.
fields.tab_content_2:
Student pricing that waits on a valid ID

The Coastal Ecology Society prices its pass three ways: $450 early bird, $600 standard and $175 for students. Students upload an ID, and the form reads its expiration date. An ID that expires before the meeting opens on June 14 puts the pass on hold, and the student is asked for a current one.
fields.tab_content_3:
One invoice covers six engineers at the group rate

Halvorsen Labs registers six engineers for Mesa DevOps Days in one submission, with an attendee section per person. Groups of five or more pay $380 a pass instead of $450. Stripe emails one $2,280 invoice to the billing contact, and each engineer gets a confirmation with their badge name.
fields.tab_content_4:
Visa letters drafted, then approved by one coordinator

Attendees from abroad tick a box when they need a letter of invitation for a visa, then add their passport name and number. Once the fee is paid, the app drafts the letter with the conference dates. Ines Varga, the program coordinator, approves each letter before it is emailed.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Conference Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the agenda, not the field list. The program decides most of what the form has to ask.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the event will use
fields.howto_step_1_des: Lay out each day as time slots, then place every parallel session in its slot with the room's seat count. Attendees choose against this grid. A session missing from it cannot be picked, and a room without a count can be overbooked.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down each pass with its price and its deadline: early bird, standard, member, student, one-day. Note which passes need proof, such as a student ID or a membership number, and what happens when that proof is missing.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Some attendees sign up alone; others arrive in a batch from a manager. Settle the group size that earns a discount, who receives the invoice and whether each person in a group gets a separate confirmation.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for the badge name and the session picks. Add meal needs or accessibility requests when a caterer or the venue will act on them. Speakers and exhibitors answer in their own sections instead of adding questions for everyone.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your notes from the first four steps into the prompt: the agenda grid, the pass prices, the group rule. Emergent builds the form with the attendee table and confirmation emails behind it. Ask for changes the same way, such as a later early-bird deadline.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Register under a made-up name with a Stripe test card and read the confirmation on a phone. Then try the cases that break forms: a student with an old ID, a group of four, a room with one seat left. Fix whatever surprises you.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Link the form from the conference site and the call for speakers, where attendees already look. A daily Slack count of new registrations by pass type shows which prices are selling and when to close the early-bird rate.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, SurveyMonkey, Cognito, Formplus, Wufoo, 123FormBuilder), a printable ILO PDF and a video. They all stop at a field list. A conference registration is harder than a one-off event sign-up: attendees pick breakouts per time slot against room limits, the price depends on date and attendee type, companies register several people on one invoice, and international attendees need visa letters. This page shows each of those as a working rule with the registrant table behind it, and answers the template, Word, PDF, free and international searches plainly.
tab_stories: A product conference runs four breakouts per afternoon slot, and a session drops off the form the moment its room's 60 seats are taken, with a Slack note to the program team.
A research association sells early-bird, standard and student passes, and holds any student pass whose uploaded ID expires before the conference opens.
An engineering firm registers six people in one submission, gets the group rate from the fifth attendee, and receives one invoice while each attendee gets their own confirmation.
An attendee flying in from abroad asks for a visa invitation letter on the form, and the letter is drafted from the passport details once the fee is paid and queued for the coordinator to approve.
